text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Ottawa to hold culture summit: Little accord likely on ways to meet challenges facing publishers, producers, broadcasters.
- Milosevic concedes victories to foes: Continue protests, opposition urges.
- Simpson liable in slashing deaths of ex-wife, friend: Grieving relatives win moral victory; Goldman's family gets US$8.5 million.
- Dingwall supports prescription plan: Medicare coverage called better way.
- Hints of crackdown cool under-age sex trade: Men on Calgary's 'baby stroll' fear dedicated efforts of MLA, ex-policeman.
- Gulf boosts bid for Clyde: Believes extra C$139-million will capture prey, but British firm rejects offer, vowing to stay independent.
- TSE reform urged: Report calls for level playing field for big and small investors.
- Hirsch, Fidelity part company: Fund star, firm mum on settlement.
- Record day for bank shares: Stocks benefit from RRSP season, positive inflation outlook.
- Cable assails phone invasion: Cable firms say Bell and Telus' trials of television services are really a commercial rollout and an intrusion on their turf.
- Gulf closes in with sweetened bid for Clyde.
